plan.G: After research closes, retrieve each tree’s evidence and select only correctly validated candidates using the official geometric-mean kernel-time objective. Build and freshly compile/check/measure combinations in the permitted files; do not assume gains are additive. Independently confirm the best candidate under the official protocol and keep the best confirmed program. Do not launch further research trees.
plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the O(N²) interaction loop offers three complementary opportunities—less arithmetic per pair, CTA-level source reuse, and register-level reuse across multiple targets. Keep these axes isolated during research so G can measure their combinations rather than assume additive gains. The supplied baseline is valid and correct, with a mean of 0.0018532571 s over three timing repetitions; only aggregate timing is available, so it does not establish per-size behavior or a specific bottleneck.

children.objective: Optimize pair arithmetic in the existing one-output-per-thread global-memory traversal. Explore accumulating acceleration directly to avoid target-mass multiply/divide and using rsqrtf-based inverse-distance powers; consider removing the self-interaction branch only with finite-safe handling. Do not add shared-memory staging or multi-target ownership. Write only src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json. Preserve the specified physics, update order, exact masses, and complete output; pass all oracle checks for arbitrary sizes, including tails, coincident positions, zero/negative dt, and the isolated extreme-mass case. Judge candidates by the official geometric-mean kernel time.
children.subject: Reduce per-pair arithmetic while preserving the scalar traversal

children.objective: Explore cooperative shared-memory tiles of source particles, with one target per thread and all N sources covered for every target. Keep the baseline interaction arithmetic and do not introduce multi-target ownership. Tune tile/block configuration within the 49152-byte shared-memory limit; ensure partial target blocks still participate correctly in barriers and all source/target tails are handled. Write only src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json. Preserve the full interface and correctness requirements, then measure against the official objective.
children.subject: CTA-level source reuse through shared-memory tiling

children.objective: Explore bounded register blocking: each thread computes a small fixed batch of target particles and reuses each globally loaded source particle across that batch. Keep global-memory traversal and baseline pair arithmetic; do not add shared-memory staging. Choose block and items_per_block consistently with the required grid formula, bound per-thread register use, and handle arbitrary N and partial batches without benchmark-size assumptions. Write only src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json; preserve complete state, exact masses, and all correctness requirements, then measure the official objective.
children.subject: Register-level source reuse with multiple targets per thread

data.analysis: Keep N=3 and all role identities, but sharpen the experiments. T2 and T3 both hypothesize source-load reuse, while the original loop has all lanes visiting the same source index; hardware caching may already amortize those reads. T3 also mixes output batching with launch geometry. Add matched controls so results can distinguish those effects. T1 can isolate the diagonal-branch change from its arithmetic rewrite. These are research focuses, not bans on later correctness-preserving combinations.

revisions.objective: Use the existing one-output-per-thread global traversal to test distinct inner-loop hypotheses. First compare the original diagonal skip with split ranges j<i and j>i, keeping the original force arithmetic; separately test acceleration accumulation and rsqrtf-based inverse-distance powers. Measure these individually before trying combinations. Preserve the specified softening, update order, exact masses, and finite outputs; check arbitrary sizes, coincident positions, zero/negative dt, and the isolated extreme-mass case. Write only the permitted kernel and launch files and evaluate with the official correctness and timing protocol.
revisions.subject: Isolate diagonal handling from per-interaction arithmetic changes

revisions.objective: Test CTA-level source staging with one target per thread, keeping the original interaction arithmetic as a control. Compare global traversal and shared-memory staging at matched block configuration; stage only x, y, z, and mass as a compact alternative to staging full Particle records. Since source-load reuse may already be served by the hardware cache, treat benefit as a hypothesis. Tune within the shared-memory limit, handle source and target tails, and ensure every thread reaches required barriers. Write only the permitted kernel and launch files; validate and time with the official protocol. Combinations with other ideas remain available after isolated tests.
revisions.subject: Measure shared-memory staging against cached global reads

revisions.objective: Keep global-memory traversal and baseline pair arithmetic as controls. First measure one-output-per-thread launch configurations with items_per_block equal to block; then test bounded per-thread target batches, reusing each source record across the batch. This separates launch-geometry effects from register-level reuse. Respect the required grid formula, bound register use, and handle arbitrary sizes and partial batches without specializing to benchmark sizes. Write only the permitted kernel and launch files; validate and time with the official protocol. Further correctness-preserving combinations are not excluded.
revisions.subject: Separate launch-geometry tuning from register-blocked target reuse

data.shared_assumptions: All three topics assume the direct all-pairs kernel is best improved inside its per-target loop; none has measured which resource limits runtime. Shared-memory and register batching both predict benefit from source reuse, but the original warp-uniform source-index accesses may already be cached or broadcast. The only supplied baseline timing is an aggregate mean over three repetitions, without per-size timings or profiling data. Treat each mechanism as a hypothesis and compare matched controls; keep combined experiments possible after isolated variants.
